name: prompt-composer
summary: The image generator's composer: a prompt box, a model chip, an aspect-ratio chip, a 1 to 4 image stepper and the lime Generate button showing what the request will cost in credits.
useWhen: Someone writes a prompt and starts an image generation, such as at the bottom of an image studio or under a studio home hero.
The cost depends on the model and the number of images, and people should see it before they spend credits.

alternatives.name: textarea
alternatives.when: you only need the borderless prompt field inside a surface you already built

alternatives.name: select
alternatives.when: a settings panel needs one more chip, such as quality, without the whole composer

rules.do: Keep the credit cost on the Generate button, so it updates the moment someone changes the model or the number of images.
rules.dont: Hide the cost in a tooltip or a separate line, where people find out what they spent only after pressing Generate.

rules.do: Leave the model, aspect-ratio and image-count chips neutral; Generate is the only lime element in the composer.
rules.dont: Paint a chip or a second button lime. Lime marks the one main action, Generate, and a second one dilutes it.

rules.do: Place one composer per screen, docked where the results appear.
rules.dont: Repeat the composer in several cards; people lose track of which settings they are about to spend credits on.

rules.do: Pass `creditBalance` so a request the person cannot afford disables Generate and says how to fix it.
rules.dont: Let Generate fail after the click with a generic error about credits.

a11y: The prompt has an accessible name ("Prompt"); the placeholder is only an example of what to write.
Each chip is named for its setting ("Model", "Aspect ratio") because it shows only the chosen value.
Generate is named with its cost, such as "Generate 4 credits", so screen-reader users hear the price too.
When credits run short, the explanation is linked to the disabled button with `aria-describedby`.
Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter in the prompt generates; plain Enter adds a new line.
